doppel · a report on its own source

doppel

doppel measures architectural erosion in a Go codebase — the widening gap between the structure a project intends and the one it actually has.

Nobody erodes an architecture deliberately. Someone needs a retry loop and writes one, because finding the existing one costs more than writing it. Someone forks a handler for a second provider, and a year later only one of the two carries the bug fix. Every such edit is defensible on its own and invisible in review, because review sees a diff and erosion is a property of the whole corpus. That is why doppel reads every function in the repo at once rather than reading a change.

It fingerprints each function from its AST and cross-checks matches against call-graph context, so it finds pairs that share shape and role rather than string overlap — the kind text-based clone detection stops seeing once two copies have drifted apart. Everything runs locally and offline: no models, no network, no cache. The same source always produces the same report.

The report below is doppel run on doppel

This is not a demo corpus. It is the tool's own source, analysed by itself, regenerated from master on every push — so every pair it names can be opened in this repository and judged. The page is one self-contained file with nothing to fetch.

Map draws the corpus as a political map: each package is a polygon whose area is its share of the functions, functions are dots inside their own region coloured by learned concept, and a painted border is duplication crossing between two regions. Neighbourhood takes one function and shows its ranked neighbours with both bodies side by side and the evidence for the match.
